questions.question: To what does David ask his prayer to be compared in Psalm 141?
options: A sweet song to God, and his bowed head as a humble offering
Incense before God, and his lifted hands as the evening sacrifice
A silent vow to God, and his folded hands as a quiet prayer
A loud shout to God, and his clapping hands as a great joyful noise
questions.answer: Incense before God, and his lifted hands as the evening sacrifice

questions.question: What does David ask God to set over his mouth?
options: A lamp, and to light the path before his feet
A guard, and to keep watch over the door of his lips
A shield, and to cover his heart from the enemy
A wise teacher, and to instruct his mind in the holy law
questions.answer: A guard, and to keep watch over the door of his lips

questions.question: David says, 'Let a righteous man strike me—it is a kindness.'
Let my prayer be counted as _____ before you.
Set a _____, O LORD, over my mouth; keep watch over the door of my lips!
